title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 64 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 435–437 (Night 64, continuing directly from nights-63), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 64 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Nuzhat al-Zamān goes on with her discourse of exemplary anecdotes: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb frees a slave-herder, lives plainly while rewarding others, and refuses his daughter Ḥafṣa a share of the public money; then sayings of the early pious (al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Sufyān, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād) with a pair of verses on piety; and last the caliph ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who takes back what his Umayyad kin had held, until the night breaks off as his aunt Fāṭima comes to plead with him. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْةُ الرَّابِعَةُ وَالسِّتُّونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-layatu al-rābiʿatu wa-al-sittūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fourth and the sixty,
sentences.i: And when it was the sixty-fourth night,
sentences.n: The print drops a lām from الليلة (“the night”) and gives اللية; it is kept as printed and read as al-layatu.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ قَالَتْ قِيلَ إِنَّ عُمَرَ مَرَّ بِرَاعٍ مَمْلُوكٍ فَاسْتَبَاعَهُ شَاةً
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Nuzhata al-Zamāni qālat qīla inna ʿUmara marra bi-rāʿin mamlūkin fa-istabāʿahu shātan
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the fortunate, that Nuzhat al-Zamān said: It was said that ʿUmar passed by a herder, a owned-one, and asked him to sell him a sheep.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Nuzhat al-Zamān said: It is told that ʿUmar passed a slave who was herding sheep and asked him to sell him one.
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and أن together as one word (السَّعِيدُأَنَّ); it is kept as printed. The ʿUmar here is ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, the second caliph, not the king of the tale.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّهَا لَيْسَتْ لِي فَقَالَ أَنْتَ الْفَصْلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu innahā laysat lī fa-qāla anta al-faṣlu
sentences.l: And he said to him: Truly-she is not for-me. And he said: You are the decision.
sentences.i: He said to him, “She is not mine.” And he said, “You are the one who decides.”
sentences.n: The exchange is compressed and obscure: the print gives only these two replies, and the sense of الفصل (“the decision”, “the one who settles”) is uncertain; a word may have dropped out. It is translated as it stands.

sentences.t: فَاشْتَرَاهُ ثُمَّ أَعْتَقَهُ فَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ كَمَا رَزَقْتَنِي الْعِتْقَ الْأَصْغَرَ فَارْزُقْنِى الْعِتْقَ الْأَكْبَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-ishtarāhu thumma aʿtaqahu fa-qāla Allāhumma kamā razaqtanī al-ʿitqa al-aṣghara fa-urzuqnī al-ʿitqa al-akbara
sentences.l: And he bought him, then he freed him. And he said: O God, as You provided me the freeing the lesser, so provide me the freeing the greater.
sentences.i: He bought him and then set him free, and said, “O God, as You have granted me the lesser freedom, grant me the greater.”
sentences.n: The “greater freedom” is release from the Fire. The print ends فارزقنى with the dotless ى.

sentences.t: وَقِيلَ إِنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ كَانَ يُطْعِمُ الْحَلِيبَ لِلْخَدَمِ وَيَا كُلُ الْغَلِيظَ وَيَكْسُوهُمُ اللَّيِّنَ وَيَلْبَسُ الْخَشِنَ وَيُعْطِى النَّاسَ حُقُوقَهُمْ وَيَزِيدُ فِي عَطَائِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qīla inna ʿUmara ibna al-Khaṭṭābi kāna yuṭʿimu al-ḥalība li-al-khadami wa-yā kulu al-ghalīẓa wa-yaksūhumu al-layyina wa-yalbasu al-khashina wa-yuʿṭī al-nāsa ḥuqūqahum wa-yazīdu fī ʿaṭāʾihim
sentences.l: And it was said that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb used to feed the milk to the servants, and he eats the coarse, and clothes them in the soft, and wears the rough, and gives the people their dues, and increases in their allowances.
sentences.i: It is also told that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gave his servants milk and ate coarse food himself, clothed them in soft cloth and wore rough, gave people their full dues, and raised their allowances.
sentences.n: The print splits ويأكل into two words, ويا كل. اللّين (“the soft”) is printed with a shadda on the second lām.

sentences.t: وَأَعْطَى رَجُلًا أَرْبَعَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ وَزَادَهُ أَلْفًا
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭā rajulan arbaʿata ālāfi dirhamin wa-zādahu alfan
sentences.l: And he gave a man four thousand dirhams and added to him a thousand.
sentences.i: He once gave a man four thousand dirhams, and then added a thousand more.

sentences.t: فَقِيلَ لَهُ أَمَا تَزِيدُ ابْنَكَ كَمَا زِدْتَ هَذَا قَالَ هَذَا ثَبَتَ وَالِدُهُ يَوْمَ أُحُدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qīla lahu a-mā tazīdu ibnaka kamā zidta hādhā qāla hādhā thabata wālduhu yawma Uḥudin
sentences.l: And it was said to him: Will you not add to your son as you added to this one? He said: This one, his father stood firm on the day of Uḥud.
sentences.i: Someone said to him, “Will you not give your own son more, as you gave this man?” He said, “This man’s father stood firm on the day of Uḥud.”
sentences.n: Uḥud (625) was the battle at which many Muslims fled and a few held their ground.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ الْحَسَنُ أُتِيَ عُمَرُ بِمَالٍ كَثِيرٍ فَانْتَهَ حَفْصَةُ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ حَقُّ قَرَابَتِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla al-Ḥasanu utiya ʿUmaru bi-mālin kathīrin fa-intaha Ḥafṣatu fa-qālat lahu yā amīra al-muʾminīna ḥaqqu qarābatika
sentences.l: And al-Ḥasan said: There was brought to ʿUmar a great amount of wealth, and Ḥafṣa arrived, and she said to him: O commander of the believers, the due of your kinship!
sentences.i: Al-Ḥasan said: A great sum of money was brought to ʿUmar. Ḥafṣa came to him and said, “Commander of the Faithful, the due of your kin!”
sentences.n: فانته is printed so, with no final tā’; it is read as a slip for فانتهت “and she reached (him)”, and the sentence is translated accordingly. Ḥafṣa is ʿUmar’s daughter. Her words are elliptical: she asks that her kin be given their share.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا حَفْصَةُ إِنَّمَا أَوْصَى اللَّهُ بِحَقِّ قَرَابَتِي وَأَمَّا مَالُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَلَا يَا حَفْصَةُ قَدْ أَرْضَيْتِ قَوْمَكِ وَأَغْضَبْتِ أَبَاكِ فَقَامَتْ تَجُرُّ ذَيْلَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā Ḥafṣatu innamā awṣā Allāhu bi-ḥaqqi qarābatī wa-ammā mālu al-muslimīna fa-lā yā Ḥafṣatu qad arḍaytī qawmaki wa-aghḍabtī abāki fa-qāmat tajurru dhaylahā
sentences.l: And he said: O Ḥafṣa, God only commanded the due of my kinship; as for the wealth of the Muslims, no. O Ḥafṣa, you have pleased your people and angered your father. And she stood, dragging her hem.
sentences.i: He said, “Ḥafṣa, God has commanded only that I give my kin their due. The wealth of the Muslims is another matter, and no. Ḥafṣa, you have pleased your people and angered your father.” And she rose and left, trailing her hem.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ تَضَرَّعْتُ إِلَي رَبِّي سَنَةً مِنَ السِّنِينَ أَنْ يُرِيَنِي أَبِي حَتَّى رَأَيْتُهُ يَمْسَحُ الْعَرَقَ عَنْ جَبِينِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ibnu ʿUmara taḍarraʿtu ilā rabbī sanatan mina al-sinīna an yuriyanī abī ḥattā raʾaytuhu yamsaḥu al-ʿaraqa ʿan jabīnihi
sentences.l: And the son of ʿUmar said: I besought my lord for a year of the years that he show me my father, until I saw him wiping the sweat from his brow.
sentences.i: Ibn ʿUmar said: For a whole year I besought my Lord to show me my father, until at last I saw him wiping the sweat from his brow.

sentences.t: فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا حَالُكَ يَا وَالِدِي فَقَالَ لَوْلَا رَحْمَةُ رَبِّي لَهَلَكَ أَبُوكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qultu lahu mā ḥāluka yā wālidī fa-qāla lawlā raḥmatu rabbī la-halaka abūka
sentences.l: And I said to him: What is your state, O my father? And he said: Were it not for the mercy of my lord, your father would have perished.
sentences.i: I said to him, “Father, how are you?” He said, “Had it not been for my Lord’s mercy, your father would have perished.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ اسْمَعْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ الْفَصْلَ الثَّانِيَ مِنَ الْبَابِ الْأَوَّلِ مِنْ أَخْبَارِ التَّابِعِينَ وَسَائِرِ الصَّالِحِينَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat Nuzhatu al-Zamāni ismaʿ ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu al-faṣla al-thāniya mina al-bābi al-awwali min akhbāri al-tābiʿīna wa-sāʾiri al-ṣāliḥīna
sentences.l: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said: Hear, O king the fortunate, the chapter the second from the gate the first, from the reports of the followers and the rest of the righteous.
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said: Hear, O fortunate king, the second section of the first part, on the reports of the Followers and the other righteous.
sentences.n: The Followers (التابعون) are the generation after the Prophet’s Companions. Here الفصل is a “section” of her discourse, not the “decision” of the earlier anecdote.

sentences.t: قَالَ الْحَسَنُ الْبَصْرِيُّ لَا تَخْرُجُ نَفْسُ ابْنِ آدَمَ مِنَ الدُّنْيَاً إِلَّا وَهُوَ يَتَأَسَّفُ عَلَى ثَلَٰثَةِ أَشْيَاءَ عِلْمُ تَمَتُّعِهِ بِمَا جَمَعَ وَعَدَمِ إِدْرَاكِهِ لِمَا أَمَّلَ وَعَدَمِ اسْتِعْدَادِهِ بِكَثْرَةِ الزَّادِ لِمَا هُوَ قَادِمٌ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: qāla al-Ḥasanu al-Baṣrīyyu lā takhruju nafsu ibni Ādama mina al-dunyā illā wa-huwa yata-assafu ʿalā thalāthati ashyāʾa ʿilmu tamattuʿihi bi-mā jamaʿa wa-ʿadami idrākihi li-mā ammala wa-ʿadami istiʿdādihi bi-kathrati al-zādi li-mā huwa qādimun ʿalayhi
sentences.l: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: The soul of the son of Adam does not go out from the world but that he grieves over three things: [knowledge] of his enjoying what he gathered, and the lack of his attaining what he hoped for, and the lack of his preparing, with abundance of provision, for what he is coming upon.
sentences.i: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: No child of Adam leaves this world without grieving over three things: that he did not enjoy what he amassed, that he did not attain what he hoped for, and that he did not provide enough for the journey to what awaits him.
sentences.n: The print has علم “knowledge” where the list needs عدم “lack” (the next two items begin with عدم); it is probably a misprint, and the sentence is translated as if it read “lack of his enjoying”. الدنياً is printed with a fatḥatān on the final alif.

sentences.t: وَقِيلَ لِسُفْيَانَ أَيَكُونُ الرَّجُلُ زَاهِدًا وَيَكُونُ لَهُ مَالٌ قَالَ نَعَمْ إِذَا كَانَ مَتَى ابْتُلِيَ صَبَرَ وَإِذَا أُعْطِيَ شَكَرَ
sentences.tr: wa-qīla li-Sufyāna a-yakūnu al-rajulu zāhidan wa-yakūnu lahu mālun qāla naʿam idhā kāna matā ubtuliya ṣabara wa-idhā uʿṭiya shakara
sentences.l: And it was said to Sufyān: Can the man be an ascetic and have wealth? He said: Yes, if he is, whenever he is tried, patient, and when he is given, grateful.
sentences.i: Sufyān was asked, “Can a man be an ascetic and still own wealth?” He said, “Yes, if he is patient whenever he is tried, and grateful whenever he is given.”

sentences.t: وَقِيلَ لَمَّا حَضَرَتْ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ شَدَّادٍ الْوَفَاةُ أَحْضَرَ وَالِدَهُ مُحَمَّدًا فَأَوْصَاهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا بُنَيَّ
sentences.tr: wa-qīla lammā ḥaḍarat ʿAbda Allāhi ibna Shaddādin al-wafātu aḥḍara wālidahu Muḥammadan fa-awṣāhu wa-qāla lahu yā bunayya
sentences.l: And it was said that when death came to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād, he brought his father Muḥammad, and charged him, and said to him: O my little son,
sentences.i: It is told that when ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād was dying, he sent for his son Muḥammad, gave him his charge, and said, “My son,”
sentences.n: The print has والده, “his father”, where the sense (he calls him “my son”) needs ولده, “his son”; the vocalisation follows the print and the translation follows the sense.

sentences.t: إِنِّي لَأَرَى دَاعِيَ الْمَوْتِ قَدْ دَعَالِي فَعَلَيْكَ بِتَقْوَى اللَّهِ فِى السِّرِّ وَالْعَلَانِيَةِ وَالشُّكْرِلِلَّهِ وَصِدْقِ الْحَدِيثِ
sentences.tr: innī la-arā dāʿiya al-mawti qad daʿālī fa-ʿalayka bi-taqwā Allāhi fī al-sirri wa-al-ʿalāniyati wa-al-shukri li-Allāhi wa-ṣidqi al-ḥadīthi
sentences.l: Truly I indeed see the caller of death, he has called for me; so upon you be the fear of God in the secret and the open, and the thanks to God, and the truth of speech;
sentences.i: “I see the summoner of death, and he has called me. So hold to the fear of God in secret and in public, to thankfulness to God, and to truthful speech;
sentences.n: The print runs والشكر and لله together (والشكرلله). عَلَيْكَ بِـ is the idiom “hold fast to”.

sentences.t: فَالشُّكْرُ يُؤْذِنُ بِازْدِيَادِ النِّعَمِ وَالتَّقْوَى خَيْرُ زَادٍ كَمَا قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-al-shukru yuʾdhinu bi-izdiyādi al-niʿami wa-al-taqwā khayru zādin kamā qāla baʿḍuhum shiʿrun
sentences.l: for thanks gives notice of the increase of the blessings, and the fear-of-God is best provision, as some of them said, verse:
sentences.i: for gratitude announces an increase of blessings, and piety is the best of provisions, as one of them said in verse:”

sentences.t:
وَلَسْتُ اَرَى السَّعَادَةَ جَمْعَ مَالٍ * وَلٰكِنَّ التَّقِيَّ هُوَ السَّعِيدُ
وَتَقْوَى اللهِ خَيْرُ الزَّادِ حَقًّا * وَعِنْدَ اللهِ لِلْاَتْقَى مَزِيدُ
sentences.tr:
wa-lastu arā al-saʿādata jamʿa mālin * wa-lākinna al-taqiyya huwa al-saʿīdu
wa-taqwā Allāhi khayru al-zādi ḥaqqan * wa-ʿinda Allāhi li-al-ataqā mazīdu
sentences.l:
And I do not see happiness (to be) a gathering of wealth, * but the God-fearing, he is the happy;
and the fear-of-God is the best of provision, truly, * and with God, for the most God-fearing, there is increase.
sentences.i:
I do not think happiness lies in heaping up wealth; * it is the pious who are the happy.
Piety is truly the best of provisions, * and with God the most devout will have increase.
sentences.n: The edition prints this verse pointed, and the pointing is copied as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ لِيَسْمَعِ الْمَلِكُ هَذِهِ النُّكَتَ مِنَ الْفَصْلِ الثَّانِي مِنَ الْبَابِ الْأَوَّلِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat Nuzhatu al-Zamāni li-yasmaʿi al-maliku hādhihi al-nukata mina al-faṣli al-thānī mina al-bābi al-awwali
sentences.l: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said: Let the king hear these points from the chapter the second from the gate the first.
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān said: Let the king hear these further points from the second section of the first part.

sentences.t: قِيلَ لَهَا وَمَاهِيَ قَالَتْ لَمَّا وَلِيَ عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ الْخِلَافَةَ جَاءَلِأَ هْلِ بَيْتِهِ فَأَخَذَ مَا بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَضَعَهُ فِي بَيْتِ الْمَالِ
sentences.tr: qīla lahā wa-mā hiya qālat lammā waliya ʿUmaru ibnu ʿAbdi al-ʿAzīzi al-khilāfata jāʾa li-ahli baytihi fa-akhadha mā bi-aydīhim wa-waḍaʿahu fī bayti al-māli
sentences.l: It was said to her: And what are they? She said: When ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz took charge of the caliphate, he came to the people of his house, and took what was in their hands, and put it in the house of the wealth.
sentences.i: They said to her, “And what are they?” She said: When ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz became caliph, he went to the members of his own household, took what they held, and put it into the public treasury.
sentences.n: The print runs لأهل together with the verb and splits it after the alif (جاءلا هل); it is kept as printed and reads jāʾa li-ahli. The household are the Umayyads, who had enriched themselves under earlier caliphs.

sentences.t: فَفَزِعَتْ بَنُوا أُمَيَّةَ إِلَى عَمَّتِهِ فَاطِمَةَ بِنْتِ مَرْوَانَ فَأَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِ قَائِلَةً إِنَّهُ لَا بُدَّ مِنْ لِقَائِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-fazaʿat banū Umayyata ilā ʿammatihi Fāṭimata binti Marwāna fa-arsalat ilayhi qāʾilatan innahu lā budda min liqāʾika
sentences.l: And the sons of Umayya took fright and went to his paternal aunt, Fāṭima daughter of Marwān, and she sent to him, saying: There is no avoiding meeting you.
sentences.i: The Umayyads were alarmed and went to his aunt Fāṭima, daughter of Marwān, who sent him word: “I must meet you.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَتَتْهُ لَيْلًا فَأَنْزَلَهَا عَنْ دَابَّتِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma atathu laylan fa-anzalahā ʿan dābbatihā
sentences.l: Then she came to him by night, and he brought her down from her mount.
sentences.i: Then she came to him at night, and he helped her down from her mount.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَخَذَتْ مَجْلِسَهَا قَالَ لَهَا يَا عَمَّةُ أَنْتِ أَوْلَى بِالْكَلَامِ لِأَنَّ الْحَاجَةَ لَكِ فَأَخْبِرِينِي عَنْ مُرَادِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā akhadhat majlisahā qāla lahā yā ʿammatu anti awlā bi-al-kalāmi li-anna al-ḥājata laki fa-akhbirīnī ʿan murādiki
sentences.l: And when she took her seat, he said to her: O paternal aunt, you are more entitled to speech, for the need is yours; so inform me of your aim.
sentences.i: When she had taken her seat he said, “Aunt, you have the better right to speak, since the need is yours. Tell me what you want.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْتَ أَوْلَى بِالْكَلَامِ وَرَأْيُكَ يَسْتَشِفُّ مَا يَخْفَى عَنِ الْأَفْهَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā amīra al-muʾminīna anta awlā bi-al-kalāmi wa-raʾyuka yastashiffu mā yakhfā ʿani al-afhāmi
sentences.l: And she said: O commander of the believers, you are more entitled to speech, and your opinion sees-through what is hidden from the understandings.
sentences.i: She said, “Commander of the Faithful, it is you who have the better right to speak; your judgment sees through what is hidden from other minds.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى بَعَثَ مُحَمَّدًا رَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ وَعَذَابًا عَلَى آخَرِينَ ثُمَّ اخْتَارَ لَهُ مَا عِنْدَهُ فَقَبَضَهُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿUmaru ibnu ʿAbdi al-ʿAzīzi inna Allāha taʿālā baʿatha Muḥammadan raḥmatan li-qawmin wa-ʿadhāban ʿalā ākharīna thumma ikhtāra lahu mā ʿindahu fa-qabaḍahu ilayhi
sentences.l: And ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: Truly God, the exalted, sent Muḥammad as a mercy to a people and as a punishment upon others; then He chose for him what is with Him, and took him to Himself.
sentences.i: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said, “God Most High sent Muḥammad as a mercy to some and a punishment to others; then He chose for him what is with Him, and took him to Himself.”

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night. Unlike the previous night, the print here writes her name as one word.
